parts.visual:
A massive corporation buys your startup for $50 Million. You celebrate. Then you read the contract. They are giving you $10 Million today, and keeping $40 Million hostage. You only get the remaining $40 Million if you agree to work for the corporation for the next three years.

The Trap:
1. The Earn-Out: A pricing structure where the seller must meet certain financial or operational goals *after* the acquisition to receive the full purchase price.
2. The Golden Handcuffs: Acquiring companies do not want the founder to sell the company and immediately quit to sit on a beach. They use Earn-Outs and new Vesting schedules to lock the founder in.
parts.audio: When you sell your startup, the deal is almost never paid in 100% upfront cash. Acquiring companies use Earn-Outs to force the founders to stay, essentially turning the brilliant entrepreneur back into a corporate employee.

questions.question: A startup is acquired for $20 Million. The contract includes an 'Earn-Out' stating the founders get $5M upfront, and $15M only if the product hits 1 million users by next year. Why is this extremely dangerous for the founders?
options: Because 1 million is a small number.

Because the founders no longer control the budget. The acquiring corporation can simply refuse to give the founders the marketing budget needed to hit the 1 million user goal, guaranteeing the founders never see the $15M.
questions.correct_answer: Because the founders no longer control the budget. The acquiring corporation can simply refuse to give the founders the marketing budget needed to hit the 1 million user goal, guaranteeing the founders never see the $15M.
questions.explanation: Earn-outs put the founder's payout at the mercy of corporate bureaucracy.

questions.question: Listen to the acquiring CEO. What is 'Rest and Vest'?
questions.tts_text: We bought his company, and we locked him into a 4-year vesting schedule for the payout. Now he just sits in the corner office doing absolutely nothing, playing video games, waiting for his time to expire so he can take the money.
options: Rest and Vest. A phenomenon where acquired founders lose all motivation but cannot quit without losing their massive payout. They become 'zombie employees' waiting out their contractual prison sentence.
questions.correct_answer: Rest and Vest. A phenomenon where acquired founders lose all motivation but cannot quit without losing their massive payout. They become 'zombie employees' waiting out their contractual prison sentence.
questions.explanation: This is why so many founders quit exactly on the 4-year anniversary of their acquisition.

questions.question: If a founder hates the acquiring company and quits in Year 1 of a 3-Year Earn-Out, what happens?
options: They walk away with nothing but their initial upfront cash. They legally forfeit the massive Earn-Out payout. The acquiring company gets to keep the startup and save millions of dollars.
questions.correct_answer: They walk away with nothing but their initial upfront cash. They legally forfeit the massive Earn-Out payout. The acquiring company gets to keep the startup and save millions of dollars.
questions.explanation: Acquiring companies often *want* the founders to quit early to save money.

questions.question: Why do acquiring companies insist on these 'Golden Handcuffs'?
options: To prevent brain drain. The value of the startup is often in the founder's head. If the founder leaves on Day 1, the product will likely die. The acquiring company needs time to absorb the technology.
questions.correct_answer: To prevent brain drain. The value of the startup is often in the founder's head. If the founder leaves on Day 1, the product will likely die. The acquiring company needs time to absorb the technology.
questions.explanation: They are buying the founder's brain as much as they are buying the code.

questions.question: Order the words to describe the reality of selling out:
questions.explanation: You traded the stress of survival for the boredom of corporate bureaucracy.
